name: Arnold's Golden Six
author: Arnold Schwarzenegger's early routine
structure: The same six exercises three times a week: squat 4x10, wide-grip bench press 3x10, chin-ups for three sets of as many as possible, behind-the-neck press 4x10, barbell curl 3x10, sit-ups for three or four sets.
progression: Add load once the reps asked for are done. No deload is defined.
adapt: The chin-ups and sit-ups are bodyweight work: in the app they progress by reps and then sets.
caveats: Minimal and easy to learn. The behind-the-neck press asks for shoulder mobility many people do not have; an overhead press in front is the usual replacement. Only the outline was checked.

name: HST (Hypertrophy-Specific Training)
author: Bryan Haycock
structure: Full body three times a week with one or two sets an exercise. Two weeks of 15s, two of 10s, two of 5s, and two more of 5s with slow lowering.
progression: Inside each two-week block the load rises by a fixed step every session and reaches the rep max for that block on its last day. A week off follows the cycle.
adapt: Written out as an eight-week cycle. The load rises every session, so the three days of a week are three routines with the same exercises. Slow lowering in the last two weeks is advice; the plan does not carry tempo.
caveats: About eleven exercises a session, so long sessions, the 15s most of all. Two sets an exercise rely on the frequency.

name: Jeff Nippard Fundamentals Hypertrophy Program
author: Jeff Nippard
structure: Compound-first hypertrophy training with effort rising week by week, sold in full-body and upper/lower versions.
progression: RPE with double progression. A paid programme: its rules were not available to check.
adapt: The app does not raise effort week by week. Nothing beyond the product page is known about this programme, so its details cannot be laid out from here.
caveats: Paid. Only its existence and outline are confirmed.

name: SBS Hypertrophy Template
author: Greg Nuckols
structure: Built like the SBS strength templates with higher rep ranges and a self-adjusting last set.
progression: A training max moved by an open set or by reps in reserve, through three blocks, with deloads in weeks 7, 14 and 21.
adapt: Built on a training max adjusted every week, with percentages that change through three blocks. The app has neither.
caveats: Its self-adjustment is well regarded; the spreadsheet is complex. Only the outline was checked.

name: Lyle McDonald Generic Bulking Routine
author: Lyle McDonald
structure: Upper/lower split, each trained twice a week with the same session both times: compound lifts for 6-8 reps, isolation work for 10-15.
progression: Start at the bottom of the rep range; when every set reaches the top, add about 2.5 kg (5 lb) and go back to the bottom.
caveats: A moderate-volume, twice-a-week template written for a calorie surplus; recovery is tight when cutting. Only the outline was checked, and no deload was found in the source.

name: PHUL
author: Brandon Campbell
structure: Four days: an upper and a lower power day at 3-5 reps, an upper and a lower hypertrophy day at 8-12.
progression: When every set reaches the top of its rep range, add 2.5 kg (5 lb) and return to the bottom. No deload is built in; a week at about half the load around week six is the usual advice once fatigue builds.
adapt: A lift that appears on both a power and a hypertrophy day progresses separately in each routine. The easy week is advice; the plan does not change for it.
caveats: Each muscle twice a week and easy to follow. The lower power day holds both squat and deadlift, and the programme has no rule for a miss.

name: Reddit PPL (Metallicadpa)
author: u/metallicadpa (r/Fitness)
structure: Pull, push, legs, twice a week. Pull days lead with deadlift or barbell row in turn, push days with bench press or overhead press in turn, for four sets of five and an open fifth; leg days squat for two sets of five and an open third. Accessories for 3x8-12.
progression: Main lifts add 2.5 kg a session (5 kg for the deadlift) and take 10 % off after three misses at one weight. Accessories work up their rep range before the load moves.
adapt: With six days the two pull, push and leg days are six routines, so the alternating main lifts keep their own days. On `greyskull` the app resets after one miss rather than three; `linear` keeps the three misses and gives up the open last set. Accessories go on `double`.
caveats: The most used push/pull/legs on Reddit. Six days is a lot for a true beginner, and the legs get less work than the upper body.

name: Coolcicada PPL
author: Coolcicada (bodybuilding.com forum)
structure: Push, pull and legs twice a week each: heavy compound lifts followed by higher-rep isolation work. The deadlift on pull days is optional.
progression: A small step up whenever the reps asked for are done. No open sets, RPE or percentages.
caveats: Plain and direct. Nothing in it deals with stalls or the long run. Only the outline was checked.

name: 4-Day Split (generic template)
author: a common template with no single author
structure: The body spread over four days, one or two large muscle groups a day; it can also be laid out as two upper and two lower days.
progression: Double progression in most versions; the versions differ.
caveats: The body-part version trains each muscle once a week. Only its existence and outline are confirmed; there is no single source for its rules.

name: Shortcut to Size
author: Jim Stoppani
structure: A body-part split in three four-week phases. The rep range changes every week, from high reps down to low, and then the phase repeats.
progression: Each phase comes back to the high reps with more load than the last.
adapt: Its weekly change of rep range can be written out as a cycle. Its supersets and drop sets later on, and its exact ranges, are not known from here.
caveats: A popular commercial programme, with supersets and drop sets later on. Only its existence and outline are confirmed.

name: 5-Day Bro Split
author: bodybuilding tradition, no single author
structure: One body part a day: chest, back, legs, shoulders, arms.
progression: Double progression in most versions; the versions differ.
caveats: Each muscle once a week, which is usually held to be less efficient than twice. Only its existence and outline are confirmed; there is no single source for its rules.

name: Kong: Savage Size in 12 Weeks
author: Alexander Bromley
structure: A body-part split training each part twice a week, in three four-week blocks: isolation first at 12-20 reps with volume building; compounds first in a 12-10-8-5 pyramid; a reverse pyramid with overload variations.
progression: The first block adds sets week by week; later blocks raise intensity. No clear deload rule in the source.
adapt: The exercise order, rep schemes and number of sets change from block to block and week to week; the app trains the same week until the plan is changed.
caveats: Sessions of about 75 minutes; results lean on a calorie surplus.

name: PHAT
author: Layne Norton
structure: Five days: an upper and a lower power day at 3-5 reps, then hypertrophy days for back and shoulders, for legs, and for chest and arms. Each hypertrophy day opens with fast sets at about 65-70 % of the power-day load.
progression: Double progression. Every 6-12 weeks, one to three easier weeks at 60-70 % of the usual loads.
adapt: Written as a cycle, the fast sets are planned as their own exercise entry at about 65-70 % of the power-day load, and the easier weeks are weeks of the cycle.
caveats: Each muscle twice a week at high volume. Five days asks a lot of recovery and is hard to keep up when cutting.

name: Arnold Split
author: Arnold Schwarzenegger
structure: Chest and back, shoulders and arms, legs, run through twice a week. Chest and back on one day allows antagonist supersets.
caveats: High volume and long sessions; it needs good recovery. Only the outline was checked, and no deload rule was found.

name: Renaissance Periodization-style hypertrophy template
author: Mike Israetel, James Hoffmann
structure: Mesocycles of four to six building weeks and a deload week. Each starts near the least volume that works, one to three reps from failure, and adds sets week by week from how sore, pumped and strong the lifter was.
progression: About one more set a muscle group each week, with effort moving closer to failure, until performance drops; then a week at about half the volume and lower intensity, and a new cycle.
adapt: Written as a cycle: sets added week by week within the weekly ceilings, effort moving closer to failure in the week's line of intent, and the easier week as a week of its own. How fast sets are added is decided from the log as the weeks are trained.
caveats: A complete system. Its volume landmarks are hard to pin down for one person. Only the outline was checked.
